title: 1968 AHSME Problem 30
statement: Convex polygons \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are drawn in the same plane with \(n_1\) and \(n_2\) sides, respectively, \(n_1\leq n_2.\) If \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) do not have any line segment in common, then the maximum number of intersections of \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) is:

solutions.text:
Each side of \(P_1\) lies on a line, and its intersection with the convex region \(P_2\) is a single segment or empty. Thus that side crosses the boundary of \(P_2\) at most twice. Across \(n_1\) sides there are at most \(2n_1,\) and a suitable thin convex \(n_1\)-gon crossing a convex \(n_2\)-gon attains this bound.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: A line segment can enter and leave a convex polygon at most once
Apply that bound to each side of the polygon with fewer sides
